findings.claim: SQM has established a new joint venture entity called Novandino Litio (also referred to as Nova Andino Litio) in partnership with the Chilean state-owned mining company CODELCO.
findings.evidence_quote: The first quarter of 2026 marked our first full quarter operating alongside CODELCO through our partnership Nova Andino Litio, and the results underscore the strength of this partnership.
findings.so_what: This partnership represents a critical shift in how SQM's lithium operations are governed; autonomous drone solutions must align with the operational standards of both SQM and CODELCO.

findings.claim: Carlos Díaz O. was appointed as the Chief Executive Officer of Novandino Litio in June 2024, having previously served as VP of Operations for Potassium and Lithium.
findings.evidence_quote: In 2019, he became Vice President of Operations, Potassium and Lithium and assumed his current role in June 2024.
findings.so_what: As the CEO of the specific entity managing the Atacama lithium partnership, Díaz is a primary stakeholder for high-level operational technology decisions like autonomous inspection.

findings.claim: The Salar de Atacama mine is operated by the subsidiary Sociedad Química y Minera (SQM) Salar de Atacama S.A., which is owned by the parent company.
findings.evidence_quote: Operating Company: Sociedad Química y Minera (SQM) Salar de Atacama S.A. Mine Owner: Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile S.A.
findings.so_what: Sales efforts for the Atacama Desert should target the leadership of this specific operating subsidiary while maintaining alignment with the parent company's executive suite.

findings.claim: Pablo Altimiras C. serves as the CEO of the Iodine-Plant Nutrition Division, a role he assumed in June 2024 after leading the Lithium and Iodine businesses.
findings.evidence_quote: In October 2018, he became Vice President of Lithium and Iodine Businesses and assumed his current role in the Company in June 2024.
findings.so_what: Altimiras oversees a major industrial division that likely shares the same desert operating environment, offering a secondary entry point for drone-based inspection.

findings.claim: Ricardo Ramos R. has served as the Chief Executive Officer of SQM since January 2019, following a long career in finance and corporate services within the company.
findings.evidence_quote: In 1989, he joined SQM as Finance Advisor and served as Chief Financial Officer and Vice President of Corporate Services from 1994 until 2018, before assuming his current role in January 2019.
findings.so_what: The lead likely reports through a chain that terminates with Ramos; his long tenure suggests a preference for internal operational continuity and proven ROI.

findings.claim: Felipe Smith is the executive heading the Lithium & Potassium division, which is currently SQM's largest revenue-generating segment.
findings.evidence_quote: Felipe Smith heads the critical Lithium & Potassium division, overseeing what has become SQM's largest revenue segment.
findings.so_what: Smith is a key executive for the lead's division; autonomous drone operations that improve efficiency in this high-revenue segment will be highly prioritized.

findings.claim: SQM's Board includes a Safety, Health and Environment Committee, which currently includes director Antonio Gil N.
findings.evidence_quote: At the Annual General Shareholders’ Meeting held on April 24, 2025, shareholders approved the Board of Directors compensation for 2025, including the compensation for the Audit and Financial Risk Committee, Corporate Governance Committee and the Safety, Health and Environmental Committee.
findings.so_what: Autonomous drones directly support the mandate of this committee by removing personnel from hazardous desert environments, providing a safety-first justification for the purchase.

findings.claim: The Salar de Atacama mine site employed 1,640 staff and 2,775 contractors as of mid-2025, highlighting a large workforce to manage in a remote area.
findings.evidence_quote: # Employees / contractors: 1,640 employees and 2,775 contractors at the time of audit
findings.so_what: The high ratio of contractors to employees suggests a complex organizational footprint where autonomous drones can provide consistent, standardized oversight without increasing headcount.

findings.claim: SQM projects a total capital expenditure of approximately US$3 billion for the three-year period spanning 2026 to 2028.
findings.evidence_quote: We expect capital expenditures to be approximately US$3 billion over the three-year period from 2026 to 2028. The breakdown is as follows: approximately 60% for Novandino, 20% for the Iodine and Plant Nutrition Division
findings.so_what: This massive budget allocation, particularly the 60% for Novandino, indicates significant capital available for technology that improves operational efficiency in the Atacama Desert.

findings.claim: The Salar Futuro project in the Salar de Atacama is estimated to require a US$3 billion capital investment over a seven-year development cycle.
findings.evidence_quote: The project contemplates an estimated capital investment of approximately US$3 billion, to be deployed over approximately seven years following receipt of the required approvals, with the most capital-intensive phase currently expected during the third and fourth years
findings.so_what: The long-term nature and high value of this project create a sustained opportunity for autonomous inspection solutions to support construction and ongoing monitoring.

findings.claim: SQM's investment plan for 2026-2028 includes approximately US$300 million per year dedicated to sustaining capital expenditures across all divisions.
findings.evidence_quote: This estimate includes approximately US$300 million per year of sustaining capital expenditures across all divisions.
findings.so_what: A consistent US$300M annual maintenance budget provides a clear entry point for autonomous drones to replace manual, high-cost inspection and maintenance routines.

findings.claim: The Novandino joint venture plans to invest US$3 billion to increase lithium production by over 70%, targeting 470,000 metric tons annually.
findings.evidence_quote: The expansion involves a substantial $3 billion investment, and although the new production levels are expected to take years to achieve, this initiative will provide robust support for Chile's competitiveness in the global lithium market.
findings.so_what: The scale of this expansion requires advanced site security and progress monitoring that autonomous drone docks are uniquely suited to provide in remote desert environments.

findings.claim: SQM has committed between US$450 million and US$500 million for the expansion of the Mt Holland lithium project.
findings.evidence_quote: Construction of a second concentrator is expected to commence in the second half of year 2027, with the first spodumene concentrate production volumes from the expansion expected in the first half of year 2030. SQM's share of capital expenditure for the project is estimated to be between US$450 million and US$500 million
findings.so_what: While this project is in Australia, it demonstrates SQM's willingness to commit large-scale Capex to international lithium expansion and infrastructure.

findings.claim: SQM's capital expenditures for the year ended December 31, 2025, reached US$876.7 million, focused on strategic expansion projects.
findings.evidence_quote: During 2025, capital expenditures were focused primarily on continuing strategic projects aimed at expanding production capacity across the three business segments. Total investment reached approximately US$876.7 million

positioning.thesis: Position FlytBase as the operational standard for the Novandino Litio joint venture to manage the 70% production increase and US$3B 'Salar Futuro' expansion without increasing human risk or contractor headcount. By automating 24/7 inspections across the Atacama's remote lithium and iodine infrastructure, SQM can maintain its low-cost producer status while directly addressing the Safety, Health and Environment Committee's mandate to remove personnel from hazardous desert conditions.

value_hooks.hook: Automated Oversight for the Novandino Litio Expansion
value_hooks.how_to_say_it: With the Supreme Court confirming the Novandino partnership and a US$3B investment to increase lithium production by 70%, FlytBase provides the scalable, pilot-free infrastructure needed to monitor this massive expansion in the Atacama without a proportional increase in high-cost contractor crews.

value_hooks.hook: Safety-First Risk Mitigation for Remote Operations
value_hooks.how_to_say_it: Given that SQM identifies operational stoppages from safety incidents as a major risk, and currently manages over 2,700 contractors in remote areas, our autonomous docks remove humans from hazardous environments while providing 24/7 emergency response and safety monitoring.

value_hooks.hook: Optimizing Linear Infrastructure and Leaching Piles
value_hooks.how_to_say_it: For your Iodine-Plant Nutrition Division's new seawater pipelines and leaching pile projects, FlytBase enables real-time, autonomous detection of leaks and structural issues, directly supporting your 2025 innovation strategy to strengthen the value-generation chain.

likely_stakeholders.why_involved: CEO of Novandino Litio; primary decision-maker for technology adoption within the critical SQM-CODELCO lithium partnership.
Head of Lithium & Potassium division; oversees the highest revenue-generating segment where autonomous efficiency gains are most impactful.
Member of the Safety, Health and Environment Committee; interested in technologies that reduce personnel exposure to hazardous desert conditions.
CEO of Iodine-Plant Nutrition Division; relevant for drone applications in pipeline and leaching pile monitoring.
Likely required for final sign-off on capital expenditures related to the US$300M annual sustaining capital budget.
Responsible for validating real-time monitoring techniques and R&D-led process improvements.

risks_and_objections: Integration challenges with CODELCO's operational standards within the new Novandino joint venture.
Connectivity and hardware durability concerns in the extreme environment of the Atacama Desert.
Potential preference for internal R&D solutions given SQM's US$55M annual R&D spend.
Complex procurement and legal review timelines typical of Chilean state-partnered entities.
avoid: Avoid focusing solely on the Lithium division; the Iodine-Plant Nutrition division has specific linear infrastructure needs (pipelines) that are high-value use cases.
Do not ignore the influence of CODELCO's standards in the new joint venture entity.
Avoid suggesting solutions that require on-site pilots, as the primary pain point is the cost and hazard of personnel in remote areas.
